confounds: The diagnosed/control classes are highly imbalanced: 619 diagnosed-labeled versus 5,463 control users.

Diagnosed-labeled users have substantially more retained posts, so timeline size, account activity, observation windows, and retention rules can affect diversity, repetition, and persistence measures.
Age, gender, region, platform norms, interaction style, fandom, and account type may influence pronouns, punctuation, message length, and elongation.
Heuristic separation of personal experience from quotation, jokes, lyrics, advocacy, news, replies, and third-person discussion is imperfect.
Source-order halves and quarters are persistence proxies because timestamps were unavailable; they do not establish temporal stability.
All findings explain label-associated observable divergence only; they do not establish depression, diagnosis, or causality.

caveats: The context filter is heuristic and cannot fully remove jokes, lyrics, quotations, or discussion of others.
Possessives and state verbs can reflect topic or demographic style rather than personal experience.
This is association with the label, not evidence of clinical diagnosis or causality.
findings.evidence_summary: The diagnosed-labeled group used first-person/self-oriented forms more often in every fold. The gap remained in both timeline halves, and it persisted after adjusting for log post count and after excluding several obvious non-personal contexts.
findings.prompt_guidance: Use as a low-level style/stance feature only; prefer explicit first-person forms and combinations with syntax or punctuation rather than isolated pronouns.

quantitative_support.measure: heuristically cleaned self-state/experience posts, excluding obvious quote, reply, link, lyric, and news cues

findings.signal: Higher singular self-reference and self-state phrasing

caveats: Sentence segmentation is approximate for short, fragmentary social-media posts.
Some length difference is related to higher activity and topic composition.
No direct parse-based syntactic complexity was assumed.
findings.evidence_summary: Across all folds, diagnosed-labeled timelines showed modestly longer messages, more clause-marker posts, and a higher sentence-length proxy. The effects are small but directionally consistent.
findings.prompt_guidance: Treat this as a syntactic-complexity proxy; normalize at the user level and combine with self-reference or punctuation features.

quantitative_support.measure: user-level mean tokens per sentence proxy

findings.signal: Slightly longer and more clause-bearing messages

caveats: Question marks may be rhetorical or conversational.
Negation words can occur in quotations, jokes, advocacy, or ordinary disagreement.
The measured effect is small and not clinically specific.
findings.evidence_summary: Question and negation prevalence were higher for diagnosed-labeled users in every fold, with small but persistent gaps after post-volume adjustment.
findings.prompt_guidance: Use as weak stance markers within a multifeature profile; do not interpret negation or questions as inherently depressive.
findings.signal: More question marking and slightly more negation

caveats: These markers are sensitive to age, platform conventions, and conversational style.
Repeated-character detection also captures ordinary spelling patterns.
Reply, fandom, humor, and interpersonal context may drive the difference.
findings.evidence_summary: Controls consistently showed more emphatic punctuation and repeated-character styling. This is a stable corpus-style contrast, not evidence that diagnosed-labeled users express less emotion.
findings.prompt_guidance: Consider as a corpus/platform-style feature with strong confound warnings; avoid semantic or clinical interpretation.
findings.signal: More exclamation, ellipsis, and character-elongation usage among controls

caveats: Guiraud and entropy remain partly dependent on timeline size and topic mix.
The adjusted effects were modest and not uniformly strong within individual folds.
No conclusion about vocabulary richness or clinical state should be drawn.
findings.evidence_summary: Diagnosed-labeled users had longer timelines and lower raw type-token ratios, but length-adjusted breadth and concentration measures pointed weakly toward broader, less concentrated vocabularies in every fold.
findings.prompt_guidance: Use Guiraud, entropy, concentration, or residualized diversity measures rather than raw type-token ratio; treat the effect as weak.

quantitative_support.measure: share of tokens from the 50 most frequent user-specific types

findings.signal: Raw lexical diversity is volume-confounded; adjusted breadth is mildly higher and concentration mildly lower

caveats: Could reflect observation-window, retention, account-activity, or collection differences.
Mean volume is skew-sensitive; medians overlap substantially.
Raw token counts must not be used as independent evidence.
findings.evidence_summary: Diagnosed-labeled users had more retained posts and tokens in every development fold. This is a major observable difference and a likely source of confounding for unnormalized lexical measures.
findings.prompt_guidance: Always report user-level normalized rates and include log timeline size as a control; do not treat activity itself as a psychological signal.

caveats: Median-split thresholds were chosen for corpus analysis and are not validated cutoffs.
The combination may encode demographic, topic, or platform differences.
No predictive or clinical performance is claimed from development data alone.
findings.evidence_summary: A simple exploratory combination was consistently more prevalent among diagnosed-labeled users than controls, supporting use of bundled low-level cues rather than isolated keywords.
findings.prompt_guidance: Use only as an exploratory multifeature profile and validate on the absent held-out fold; avoid threshold-based interpretation.

quantitative_support.measure: fold-wise median-split composite: high self-reference, questions, sentence length, and low ellipsis

findings.signal: Co-occurring self-reference, interrogative style, longer syntax, and lower ellipsis

negative_results: Raw type-token ratio was lower for diagnosed-labeled users in all folds, but the difference disappeared or slightly reversed after controlling for log timeline size; this is not evidence of restricted vocabulary.
Past-tense/retrospective markers were not directionally stable: post-level rates reversed in fold 4 and token-level rates were slightly lower for diagnosed-labeled users.
Second-person usage changed direction across folds, and first-person plural differences were small; no robust pronoun-family signature beyond singular self-reference.
There was no general repetition/perseveration increase: exact-post and trigram reuse were lower for diagnosed-labeled users, while bigram reuse was only slightly higher.
URLs, hashtags, emoji prevalence, and uppercase usage showed no useful stable separation.
